answers.explanation: The program waits for its I/O. The CPU idles with a wait instruction or spins in a wait loop.
That's its main weakness: no simultaneous I/O processing.
Spinning keeps the CPU hammering the shared bus, competing with the devices.
The OS indexes into it to find and update a device's entry when an interrupt arrives.
The system call puts it to sleep until the OS sees the transfer-done interrupt.
Each device has its own entry and its own queue of waiting requests.
Keeping the CPU and all the devices busy at once is worth the bookkeeping.
